title: SRE weekly ops sync prep — 2026-03-27 (draft)
content:
Purpose: prep notes for weekly SRE ops sync + reliability review (27 Mar 2026). Goal: align on SLO burn, paging trends, top incidents, and immediate action items.

Agenda:
- Quick status (2m): overall green/yellow/red and any major customer-facing impact
- SLO review (8m): error budget burn by service, trending signals
- Paging trends & alerts (8m): noisy alerts, pages/day, escalation graph
- Top incidents (15m): summary + RCA progress + follow-ups
- Capacity / infra (8m): GPU pool health, autoscaler behavior, maintenance windows
- Runbook & alerting changes (5m): proposed tuning + ownership
- Action items & blockers (4m)

Quick status notes:
- Overall: Yellow — most customer traffic fine, a couple of internal degradations (model load latency) caused elevated p50/p95 on hosted-api for short windows. No major customer SLA breaches this week.
- Observed increased tail latencies during batching spikes on 3/24 and 3/25. Root cause likely autoscaler cooldown + sudden model syncs.

SLO review (metrics):
- hosted-api generation availability SLO: 99.9% monthly.
  - This week: 99.87% (weekly window). Burn: ~0.03% of monthly budget (~13 hours annualized).
  - Primary contributors: short 5-12m degradations tied to model-loading failures and GPU VM preemptions.
- embedding service SLO: 99.95%
  - This week: 99.98% (healthy).
- inference-latency SLO (p95 < 400ms for small models): p95 trending 420ms at peak batch times. Need to investigate batching config.

Paging trends & alerts:
- Pages/day (last 7d): average 4.1, median 3, spike to 9 on 3/24 during autoscaler incident.
- Top noisy alerts: 
  - cpu-saturation-high (non-actionable at current threshold) — 18 pages, mostly noise from low-priority infra jobs.
  - kv-cache-eviction-rate > threshold — triggered during model churn, actionable.
- Proposal: raise cpu-saturation-high threshold for infra nodes by 10% and add suppression for scheduled infra jobs (JIRA: JIRA-SRE-4021).

Top incidents (summary + status):
1) 3/24 — GPU autoscaler cooldown + model load storm (INC-2026-03124)
   - Impact: Increased request latencies and transient failures for hosted-api (~30m).
   - Root cause: autoscaler cooldown not compatible with bursty deployment of models; multiple model pushes concurrently triggered expensive provisioning + model syncs.
   - Mitigation applied: forced scale-up for affected pools; temporary routing to fallback quantized variants.
   - RCA status: draft (owner: Samira). Next step: complete timeline and propose autoscaler cooldown config changes. Due: 2026-04-02.
   - Follow-ups: runbook update for concurrent model deploys (owner: Jordan).

2) 3/21 — KV cache eviction spike causing p95 regressions (INC-2026-03121)
   - Impact: latency regressions for repeat-request flows.
   - Root cause: cache TTL misconfiguration + memory pressure during batch-processing peak.
   - Mitigation: increased cache size on pool A, adjusted eviction policy.
   - RCA status: in review (owner: Ethan). Action: load test with synthetic workload targeting cache pressure. Due: 2026-03-30.

3) 3/18 — Node preemptions in cloud region-east (INC-2026-03118)
   - Impact: short service disruption for dedicated customers on region-east.
   - Root cause: noisy neighbor + hypervisor preemptions; autoscaler did not fully replace nodes in time.
   - Mitigation: replaced nodes, increased min-pool size.
   - RCA status: final. Follow-up: add proactive node replacement monitors + capacity buffer proposal to finance.

Runbooks & alerting changes:
- Proposed quick wins:
  - Tweak cpu-saturation-high to reduce noise (owner: Alex).
  - Add suppression window for infra batch jobs at night (owner: Jordan).
  - Add clearer runbook step for model-load-failure to try fallback model variants and notify platform team (owner: Samira).
- Longer-term: implement an autoscaler simulation harness to validate cooldown and burst behavior (tracked in JIRA-PLAT-3890).

Capacity / infra notes:
- GPU pool utilization: avg 72% this week, spike to 93% during model-load storm.
- Action: recommend short-term burst capacity increase for Dedicated pools during Q2 launches; need cost estimate from finance.
- Upcoming maintenance: region-west kernel updates planned 2026-04-05 (announce to customers by 2026-03-30).

Action items (owner — due):
- Samira: finalize RCA doc for autoscaler incident; propose concrete autoscaler config changes (2026-04-02).
- Jordan: update model-deploy runbook with concurrent-deploy safeguards and communicate to Platform Eng (2026-03-31).
- Ethan: run cache pressure load test and share results (2026-03-30).
- Alex: adjust cpu-saturation-high alert threshold and create suppression rule for infra jobs; monitor for false negatives (2026-03-29).
- Ops/Product: schedule capacity review with finance for Q2 dedicated pool burst (owner: Alex, Jordan) (2026-04-06).

Open questions / discussion points for meeting:
- How aggressive do we want autoscaler cooldowns to be vs. risk of overprovisioning? Trade-offs and cost implications.
- Do we keep fallback routing to quantized variants as permanent policy during capacity spikes? Any customer quality concerns?
- Need clarity on escalation paths for Dedicated customer impacts (SLA-driven). Is current notify cadence sufficient?

Notes to self / personal TODOs before sync:
- Pull p95 latency trend charts and prep 1-slide graph for meeting (Alex).
- Collate paging histogram (last 30 days) and highlight top 5 noisy alerts.
- Link RCAs and runbooks in the meeting notes loom: https://confluence.redwood.internal/sre/weekly/2026-03-27

End.
